issues.body: After the validation loop, `check("every staged...", sorted(_staged), sorted(_staged))` compares a value with itself. Deleting the entire `for _name in sorted(_staged)` block therefore leaves this check green and preserves the pristine check count, even though no staged row is validated. The shipped solid-sdk row catches mutations that make that row invalid, but the suite does not catch deletion or conditional bypass of the newly added validation control itself. This is the value-identical/vacuous assertion shape the repository pre-flight explicitly requires authors to reject.
issues.fix_hint: Accumulate a success value only after each `_policy_row(_name, _probe)` call returns, then compare that independently produced result with the staged-row expectation. Add a non-crashing deletion/conditional-inert mutation proving the pristine and mutant runs execute the same total check count and that bypassing validation produces a line-anchored failure. Do not compare `_staged` directly with itself.
issues.title: The staged-row guard ends in a tautological check

verdict.summary: Both round-1 defects are substantively corrected: the staged row now uses a supported profile and the enrolment probe starts from an independently asserted empty value. The new staged-row validation does exercise the shipped policy under enabled=true, but its only named check is value-identical and remains green if the validation loop is deleted. That leaves the newly advertised invariant without a non-vacuous deletion guard, so one major test-validity issue remains.
